content: The Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research, established in 1982, is a non-profit organization dedicated to research and education in the field of biomedical science. It is located in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Although it operates as a financially independent entity, it maintains a close relationship with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). All members and associate members of the Whitehead Institute hold faculty positions within MIT's Biology Department. The Whitehead Institute is recognized as one of the foremost institutions in the world for genomic research. Its Center for Genome Research played a significant role in the Human Genome Project, contributing approximately one-third of the human genome sequence that was publicly announced in June 2000. In June 2003, Eli and Edythe L. Broad made a philanthropic commitment of $100 million to establish the Broad Institute. This new initiative was a collaborative effort involving the Whitehead Institute, MIT, Harvard University, and local teaching hospitals. The Broad Institute was created with the mission of advancing genomic medicine by developing innovative tools and applying them to the treatment of various diseases. The Whitehead Institute boasts a distinguished faculty, which includes Dr. Robert Weinberg, the recipient of the 1997 National Medal of Science. Additionally, eight of its faculty members are elected members of the National Academy of Sciences: Dr. Gerald Fink, Dr. Rudolf Jaenisch, Dr. Eric Lander, Dr. Susan Lindquist, Dr. Harvey Lodish, Dr. Terry Orr-Weaver, Dr. David Page, and Dr. Robert Weinberg. Three of these individuals—Dr. Fink, Dr. Lander, and Dr. Weinberg—are also members of the Institute of Medicine. Furthermore, six faculty members—Dr. Jaenisch, Dr. Fink, Dr. Lander, Dr. Lindquist, Dr. Lodish, and Dr. Weinberg—are Fellows of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. All faculty members of the Whitehead Institute are also part of MIT's Biology Department. Members hold tenured positions as full or associate professors, while associate members are on tenure-track appointments. The institute also offers an Affiliate Members program to foster additional collaboration and engagement.
